name: Proxmox_VE_Topology
description: Cluster, node and guest topology for Proxmox VE: cluster to node, node to guest.
technicalNotes:
OPTIONAL, and off by default. Applies only to a Proxmox resource -- one with the API token -- that also carries pve.topology.enabled=true (lowercase). One per cluster is enough, since it reports the whole cluster from wherever it runs. It shares the opt-in property with addERI_Proxmox_VE, which must also run on every node's resource for the nodes to be drawn, and with Proxmox_VE_GuestStatus's instance ERIs, which draw a guest that is not a resource of its own.

Emits two kinds of edge. Cluster to node, type "Cluster" -- only on a cluster; a standalone host gets no cluster vertex and no Cluster edges. Node to guest, type "Compute", the edge that matters: it lets a node's alerts explain the alerts of its guests.

Guests are matched to their own LogicMonitor resources by MAC address, read from the guest config (net0 and friends). LogicMonitor already keys a monitored resource on its MACs, so the two meet with no name matching -- a guest called "Kiosk01" whose resource is "Kiosk01 - Display" still connects. It is the identity VMware_vSphere_VirtualMachine_Topology uses. A guest with no readable MAC falls back to a synthesised key, as the VMware module does.

A vertex is drawn only if it matches a resource or a DataSource instance carrying predef.externalResourceID (confirmed 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-19). A guest that is its own resource matches once LogicMonitor's discovery has put its MAC in that resource's predef.externalResourceID, over SNMP or WMI. Every other guest is drawn through Proxmox_VE_GuestStatus, whose discovery puts the same key on the guest's instance when pve.topology.enabled is set.

Proxmox exposes no hardware UUID or MAC for a node, so each node vertex carries one synthesised key, proxmoxve--node--<node>--<ip> with the address /cluster/status reports for that node, and addERI_Proxmox_VE stamps the same key on each node's own resource from its system.ips. It needs no cluster name, so a node without the token matches with no property set, and one group can hold the nodes of every cluster. Only a node /cluster/status gives no address falls back to proxmoxve--<cluster>--<node>. Never both: the portal matches a multi-key vertex only to a resource carrying every key (2026-10-21). A node whose resource lacks the key is not drawn.

The cluster vertex, keyed proxmoxve--<cluster>, is not drawn: the portal drops a vertex that matches nothing, and a DataSource instance carrying the key is drawn with an edge to its own resource only (2026-10-21), which would misdraw the cluster. The Cluster edges are still emitted.

UNVERIFIED: the name-plus-IP node key across two clusters in one group (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-topology-node-ip-keys-design.md, section 6 item 5). A token-less node drawn through that key alone, with an edge to its guest's resource, was checked in a portal on 2026-10-22 (docs/DESIGN.md 7).

Cost: one /cluster/status, one /cluster/resources per type, and one config read per guest. That last is O(guests), which DESIGN section 2 rules out for a metric module -- but this runs hourly, and the MAC is available nowhere else.

Like the two addERI modules, this cannot be compiled or run outside a Collector: it works through com.logicmonitor.mod.Snippets (eriPreProcessor, isMac, generateTopology), whose output format LogicMonitor does not fully document. The build emits it to dist/scripts/collector-only/ for that reason.
